name: Lushootseed

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Northern Lushootseed (lush1252).

notes: Research. Salishan language of Puget Sound, Washington, written in a near-phonemic Americanist orthography. Symbols are close to IPA: č=[tʃ], c=[ts], š=[ʃ], ƛ=[tɬ], ɬ, x̌=[χ], and labialized kʷ/xʷ/gʷ/qʷ are mapped, with ʔ for glottal stop. The modifier apostrophe ʼ marks ejective/glottalized consonants; because it is written as a separate following symbol its glottalization is not fused onto the preceding stop here, and predictable stress and schwa placement remain the main PER contributors. Grapheme table checked against Bates, Hess & Hilbert (1994): no discrepancy found.

stress.notes: Northern Lushootseed (the dialect this spec models) assigns primary stress to the syllable containing the stem's first non-schwa (full) vowel, with the first syllable stressed by default when every vowel is schwa (Bates, Hess & Hilbert 1994; the Southern dialect instead defaults to the penult, which is NOT modelled here). `default_position=1` (first syllable) approximates this; it is exact when the first vowel is a full vowel and wrong when the word opens with one or more schwa syllables before the first full vowel — the schema has no 'skip schwa vowels' primitive, so that case is a documented, not silently-wrong, gap.
